sentence: This project builds fluorescent proteins that work in near-infrared light so researchers can see and control processes inside living mammalian cells and animals.
This project looks for epigenetic treatments for cocaine use disorder that hit their targets more selectively.
This project studies how lung adenocarcinoma starts and grows over space and time, using human groups, mouse models, single-cell sequencing and mathematical modeling.
This project provides noninvasive imaging of small animals for cancer researchers using many kinds of imaging scanners.
This project builds a computer-based framework that uses machine learning to personalize therapy for ventricular tachycardia.
This project uses statistical physics and networks to find disease genes linked to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
This project builds a data and statistics service that helps researchers study Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.
This project holds a conference series where researchers share work on the biological basis of aging.
This project studies bicarbonate transporters in the brain to learn how they work and to make tool compounds that target them.
This project studies early events that drive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, using human tissues, cell lines and a mouse model.
This project uses computer simulations to study how force changes the way a T cell receptor binds its target peptide.
This project studies how social functioning relates to treatment outcomes for opioid use disorder, using reports from patients and concerned significant others.
This project studies senescent cells in lungs with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, using single-cell data, deep learning tools and experiments.
This project studies how brain-derived neurotrophic factor affects a program shared by neurons and astrocytes that is reduced in schizophrenia.
This project studies how a complement receptor on endothelial cells worsens brain injury after stroke in a murine model.
This project supports early studies of environmental health, including air pollution and lung health, cancer, and the brain.
This project studies how a protein called ATR helps triple negative breast cancer grow aggressively and hide from the immune system.
This project provides cytogenetic services and cell line authentication for cancer researchers.
This project builds ways to collect and analyze cryo-electron microscopy data to show how protein complexes change shape.
This project builds a mouse model to test whether genome editing treatments reach the right organ.
